summary: Add an optional due date to tasks and list overdue open tasks first.
approach: As before, with the answers applied: due dates in the past are allowed, and only open tasks count as overdue.
steps: Add migration 0007_add_task_due_date with a nullable due_date column
Add dueDate to the Task model, the create and update request types and TaskValidator
Sort GET /tasks: open overdue tasks first, then by due date, then by creation time
Add tests for create, update, validation and ordering (including completed overdue tasks)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A task can be created and updated with an optional due date, including one in the past
acceptanceCriteria.check: Database, unit and API tests store, validate, create and update tasks with no due date, a future date and a past date (D1, U1, A1, A2)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: GET /tasks lists open overdue tasks first; completed tasks are never overdue
acceptanceCriteria.check: An API test lists open and completed tasks with past, future and no due dates and checks the order (A3)

testPlan.proves: After migration 0007, tasks have a nullable due_date: existing tasks keep a null due date and a new one stores a past or future date
TaskValidator accepts a missing dueDate, a future ISO date and a past one, and rejects a date that isn't ISO
POST /tasks with no dueDate, a future date and a past date returns 201 with the dueDate it was sent
PATCH /tasks/:id sets a past dueDate, changes it and clears it
GET /tasks with open and completed tasks that have past, future and no due dates lists open overdue tasks first, then by due date; completed tasks are never overdue
testPlan.replaces: 'GET /tasks lists tasks newest first', which expects the old order

skippedLayers.reason: No client code in this change (the web client is a follow-up)
No user flow changes until the web client shows due dates
